messages.author: e13072fd07a5d80a
messages.subject: Saving data
parts:
I would like to add a feature to my app where the user inputs data.  The data is then saved to a server, and can be accessed in the future through a dropdown menu.  From what I understand the shiny server is read-only and the user is not able to save data.  Are there any relatively simple solutions to this? 

 Thanks again!
Josh

messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Saving data
parts:
ShinyApps will allow writes to occur to the filesystem, the only issue (and we think it is a significant one) is that if the server goes down, you would lose the data that is was previously written.  We are thinking about whether we should try and support a model of providing a simple data store that a developer could use on to store end-user information, or whether app creators would rather use their own datastores whether it is Amazon RDS, some other cloud hosted MySQLor Postgres, Amazon's Dynamo, Cloudant or some other hosted DB offering.

Would love to hear people's thoughts on this.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Saving data
parts: For simplicity reasons, I would prefer the ability to save user data directly to shiny.  I'm not very familiar with servers, so being able to save data through shiny would probably be easiest for me.  If I were to lose the user data, it obviously wouldn't be ideal, but definitely not the end of the world.  If there was a way I could download the user data periodically to backup on my own system, that would be perfect for my needs.
